1: Runaways by Brian K. Vaughan (Marvel) is a superhero drama about teenagers who learn the worst possible thing about their families. Six kids who barely know each other are stuck together during their parents' yearly get-together, until they spy on the grown-ups and discover they are a secret society of supervillains. Horrified, the kids run away and set out to stop them. It is sharp, funny, and full of heart, a good pick for readers who like found-family stories.
2: Chibi Vampire is the light novel companion to Yuna Kagesaki's manga (Tokyopop), a gentle supernatural comedy and romance. Karin Maaka comes from a family of vampires, but she is the odd one out: instead of needing blood, she makes too much of it and has to give it back to people. Things get complicated around her classmate Kenta Usui, whose bad luck makes her blood surge. It is light, sweet, and a nice extra helping for fans of the manga.
3: Torture Princess: Fremd Torturchen by Keishi Ayasato (Yen Press) is a dark fantasy with a gothic, sharp-tongued edge. After a miserable life ends in murder, Kaito Sena is summoned to another world by Elisabeth Le Fanu, the Torture Princess, who wants him as her servant. Elisabeth has been ordered to hunt down demons and their contractors, and once she finishes, she herself is to be executed. It suits readers who like grim fantasy with a strange, tender core.
4: The Betrayal Knows My Name by Hotaru Odagiri (Yen Press) is a supernatural drama about fate, loyalty, and lives that echo across centuries. Yuki Sakurai is a kind orphan who can feel other people's pain through touch. When a mysterious man named Luka appears and swears to protect him, Yuki is drawn into an ancient war between the Giou clan and the demonic Duras. Fans of moody, beautifully drawn shojo fantasy will feel right at home.
5: Hana-Kimi: For You in Full Blossom by Hisaya Nakajo (Viz Media) is a cross-dressing school comedy and romance. Mizuki Ashiya, a girl living in America, is so inspired by high jumper Izumi Sano that she moves to Japan, cuts her hair, and enrolls at his all-boys high school. Sano has given up jumping, and Mizuki is determined to help him get back to it while keeping her secret. It is goofy, warm, and packed with a lovable cast of classmates.
6: Happy Kanako's Killer Life by Toshiya Wakabayashi (Seven Seas) is an action comedy about finding the right job in the wrong line of work. Kanako is an office worker worn down by a terrible boss and a job that makes her miserable. When she quits, she stumbles into work at an assassination company, and it turns out she is surprisingly good at it. It is bright, offbeat fun for readers who like their workplace comedies with a body count.
7: Hazure Skill: The Guild Member with a Worthless Skill Is Actually a Legendary Assassin by Kennoji (Yen Press) is a fantasy action comedy. Roland was the most feared assassin around, but he has retired and wants nothing more than a quiet desk job at the adventurers' guild. His old skills keep getting him noticed anyway, no matter how hard he tries to blend in. It is easygoing fantasy fun for fans of overpowered heroes trying to live an ordinary life.
8: The Girl I Saved on the Train Turned Out to Be My Childhood Friend by Kennoji (Yen Press) is a sweet school romantic comedy. On his morning train, Ryou Takamori steps in to help a girl being harassed, then slips away without a fuss. The girl turns out to be Hina Fushimi, his childhood friend, now the most popular girl at school, and she has not forgotten him. It is a light, gentle read for fans of slow-burn high school romance.
10: Heaven Official's Blessing by Mo Xiang Tong Xiu (Seven Seas) is a sweeping fantasy romance from China, full of gods, ghosts, and old legends. Xie Lian was once a beloved crown prince who rose to heaven, but he has been banished twice and is now a laughingstock among the gods. On his third ascension, he is sent on a mission and crosses paths with a mysterious young man, who may be the most feared ghost king of all. It is rich, funny, and deeply romantic.
12: The Hero Is Overpowered but Overly Cautious by Light Tuchihi (Yen Press) is a fantasy comedy that pokes fun at the usual isekai hero. The goddess Ristarte needs a champion for a world that is extremely hard to save, so she summons Seiya Ryuuguuin, who has incredible stats. The catch is that Seiya is cautious to an absurd degree, training endlessly and preparing for every possible danger before taking a single step. It is a great pick for anyone who likes genre parody.
15: High-Rise Invasion by Tsuina Miura and Takahiro Oba (Seven Seas) is a tense action horror story. High school student Yuri Honjo suddenly finds herself on the roof of a skyscraper in a strange world of towers linked by rope bridges, where masked killers hunt anyone they find. Desperate to survive, she sets out to find her brother, who she hopes is somewhere in this world too. It moves fast and suits readers who like survival thrillers.
16: The Invisible Man and His Soon-to-Be Wife by Iwatobineko (Seven Seas) is a gentle mystery romance. A private detective who happens to be invisible takes on a new assistant, a young woman who is blind. Since neither can see the other, they get to know each other in their own way while they work through cases together. It is a quiet, cozy read for fans of tender romance with a touch of mystery.
18: The Maid I Hired Recently Is Mysterious by Wakame Konbu (Yen Press) is a romantic comedy with a small mystery at its heart. Yuuri is a young boy living alone in his big family home after losing his parents. He takes in a live-in maid named Lilith, who is kind, capable, and clearly hiding something. Their days together are full of teasing and sweetness, and it is a nice pick for readers who like gentle, warm romance.
19: O Maidens in Your Savage Season by Mari Okada and Nao Emoto (Kodansha) is a coming-of-age comedy and drama. Five girls in a high school literature club spend their days reading classic novels, until a club discussion turns to sex and suddenly no one can stop thinking about it. Each girl stumbles through crushes, embarrassment, and growing up in her own way. It is frank, funny, and honest about how confusing being a teenager can be.
20: Berserk of Gluttony by Isshiki Ichika (Seven Seas) is a dark fantasy action story. Fate Graphite works as a gate guard and is looked down on by everyone, because his only skill, Gluttony, seems useless and leaves him always hungry. Then he discovers that when he defeats someone, his skill lets him devour their power. It suits readers who like underdog heroes and grim, growing-stronger fantasy.
21: Old Boy by Garon Tsuchiya and Nobuaki Minegishi (Dark Horse) is a gripping crime thriller. A man named Goto has spent ten years locked in a small private cell, never told who put him there or why. One day he is suddenly set free, and he sets out to find the person responsible and the reason for his imprisonment. It is moody, tense, and a strong choice for readers who love a slow-burning mystery.
22: The Melancholy of Suzumiya Haruhi-chan by Puyo (Yen Press) is a cheerful gag comedy spin-off of Nagaru Tanigawa's Haruhi Suzumiya novels. Haruhi and the members of the SOS Brigade appear in a cute, chibi style, getting into short, silly misadventures that poke fun at the original series. Kyon is still the long-suffering straight man, and Haruhi is still impossible. It is a fun pick for fans who already know the characters.
23: House of Five Leaves by Natsume Ono (Viz Media) is a quiet historical drama set in Edo-period Japan. Masanosuke Akitsu is a skilled but painfully shy samurai who keeps losing work because of his timid nature. He falls in with Yaichi, a charming man who leads a gang of kidnappers called the Five Leaves, and finds himself drawn to them. It is thoughtful and character-driven, a good fit for readers who like slow, atmospheric stories.
26: Outlanders by Johji Manabe (Dark Horse) is a classic sci-fi action story with a dose of romance. When an alien empire invades Earth, photographer Tetsuya Wakatsuki ends up face to face with its leader, Princess Kahm. To everyone's surprise, the warrior princess decides Tetsuya is the man she wants to marry. It is loud, adventurous, and a fun piece of retro manga for fans of space opera.
27: Bloom Into You by Nio Nakatani (Seven Seas) is a thoughtful yuri romance. Yuu Koito has always loved romance stories, but she has never felt the way the characters do. Then she meets Touko Nanami, the admired student council member, who has never been moved by anyone either, until she meets Yuu. It is tender and honest about figuring out your feelings, a good pick for readers who like quiet, emotional love stories.
28: Blue Flag by KAITO (Viz Media) is a heartfelt high school romance and drama. Taichi Ichinose is surprised when Futaba Kuze, a shy girl he barely knows, asks for his help. She has a crush on his best friend, Toma, and she wants Taichi to help her get closer to him. As the three spend more time together, things get complicated in ways none of them expected. It is a thoughtful read for fans of realistic teen drama.
29: Immortal Rain by Kaori Ozaki (Tokyopop) is a moody action fantasy. Rain is a man who cannot die, and there is a huge bounty on his head for anyone who can manage to kill him. Machika, the granddaughter of a legendary bounty hunter, sets out after him, but finds that Rain is not who she expected. It is atmospheric and bittersweet, a good fit for readers who like quiet, sad-eyed heroes.
30: The Vision of Escaflowne by Katsu Aki (Tokyopop) is a fantasy adventure based on the anime series. Hitomi Kanzaki is an ordinary high school girl until she is pulled into Gaea, a strange world where Earth hangs in the sky. There she meets Van, a young king, and becomes caught up in a war fought with giant armored machines. It blends magic, mecha, and romance, a nice find for fans of the classic show.
31: The Weakest Tamer Began a Journey to Pick Up Trash by Tou Fukino (Seven Seas) is a gentle fantasy adventure. Ivy is a young girl whose tamer skill is rated the weakest possible, so weak that her own village treats her as a burden. She runs away to survive on her own and soon befriends a small, unusual slime. It is cozy and kind-hearted, a nice pick for readers who like slow-paced journeys and found family.
34: The World's Finest Assassin Gets Reincarnated in Another World as an Aristocrat by Rui Tsukiyo (Yen Press) is a fantasy action story. The world's best assassin is killed by the organization he served, then offered a second chance by a goddess. He is reborn as Lugh Tuatha Dé, the son of a noble family of assassins, with one task: kill the hero who is fated to destroy the world. It suits readers who like clever, calculating heroes.
37: Cat + Gamer by Wataru Nadatani (Dark Horse) is a cozy slice-of-life comedy. Riko Kozakura is a quiet office worker who spends her free time playing video games. When she takes in a cat, she approaches the whole thing like a new game, figuring out how to keep her new companion happy. It is calm and funny, a sweet pick for cat lovers and gamers alike.
38: Those Who Hunt Elves by Yu Yagami (ADV) is a fantasy comedy with a silly streak. Three people from modern Japan, an actor, an actress, and a military fan, are pulled into a fantasy world along with a tank. The spell that can send them home has been scattered across the bodies of elves, so they have to find the right elves and get a look at their skin. It is goofy road-trip fun for fans of '90s comedy.
40: Cells at Work! Code Black by Shigemitsu Harada (Kodansha) is a darker, funnier spin on the body-as-a-workplace idea. A red blood cell starts his job inside a body that smokes, drinks, and is stressed out, so every shift is a struggle. He and his fellow cells keep working, even as things seem to get worse around them. It is a clever read for adults who like dark comedy with some real science mixed in.
41: Togari by Yoshinori Natsume (Viz Media) is a supernatural action story about a chance at redemption. Tobei is a violent criminal who has ended up in hell after his death. He is offered a deal: armed with a wooden sword called Togari, he must return to the world and destroy 108 sins in 108 days. It is a fast, gritty read for fans of dark action stories.
42: Tokyo Babylon by CLAMP (Tokyopop) is a supernatural drama set in 1990s Tokyo. Subaru Sumeragi is a gentle young man who is also the head of a powerful family of spiritual mediums, solving supernatural cases around the city. He is joined by his lively twin sister Hokuto and Seishiro, a friendly veterinarian who claims to be in love with him. It is stylish and moody, a great pick for CLAMP fans.
43: Pluto: Urasawa x Tezuka by Naoki Urasawa (Viz Media) is a sci-fi mystery that retells a classic Astro Boy story. In a world where robots live alongside humans, Europol detective Gesicht, himself a robot, is investigating a string of murders. The victims are some of the most advanced robots in the world, and Gesicht realizes he may be a target too. It is thoughtful and gripping, a strong choice for readers who like crime thrillers.
45: Kaiju Girl Caramelise by Spica Aoki (Yen Press) is a lighthearted romantic comedy. Kuroe Akaishi is a shy, awkward high school girl who keeps a big secret: when her emotions run high, she turns into a giant monster. That makes things very difficult when she starts falling for Arata Minami, the most popular boy in class. It is sweet, silly fun for readers who like quirky shojo.
46: True Beauty by Yaongyi (Webtoon) is a romantic comedy from Korea. Jugyeong Lim has been teased about her looks for years, so she teaches herself to do makeup and transforms her appearance before starting at a new school. Now she is one of the most popular girls around, but she is terrified of anyone seeing her bare face. It is funny, sweet, and a nice fit for fans of school romance.
47: Kamichama Karin by Koge-Donbo (Tokyopop) is a cute magical-girl comedy. Karin Hanazono is a clumsy, unlucky girl, and her beloved cat has just died. When she receives a ring that once belonged to her late mother, she finds out it can turn her into a goddess. Karin quickly gets pulled into a world of magic and rivals. It is a bright, bouncy read for fans of classic shojo.
48: Kamikaze Kaito Jeanne by Arina Tanemura (CMX) is a magical-girl romance. Maron Kusakabe seems like an ordinary high school girl, but she is secretly the phantom thief Jeanne, the reincarnation of Joan of Arc. Her targets are paintings where demons hide, and she steals them to seal the demons away. Meanwhile, a rival thief and a new neighbor keep complicating things. It is a sparkly, heartfelt pick for fans of classic shojo.
49: Code Geass: Lelouch of the Rebellion by Majiko! (Bandai) is a sci-fi action manga based on the anime. Lelouch Lamperouge is an exiled prince living in a Japan conquered by the Britannian Empire. When a mysterious girl gives him the power of Geass, letting him command anyone to obey him, he sets out to bring down the empire himself. It is a quick, dramatic read for fans of the show.
50: Cross Game by Mitsuru Adachi (Viz Media) is a baseball story about growing up, family, and first love. Ko Kitamura is the son of a sporting goods shop owner, and he has grown up alongside the four Tsukishima sisters next door, whose family runs a batting center. Their lives are tangled together through childhood, school, and the game of baseball. It is quiet, funny, and very moving, a great pick even for readers who do not follow sports.
52: Keep Your Hands Off Eizouken! by Sumito Oowara (Dark Horse) is a creative comedy about making anime. Midori Asakusa is full of wild ideas, Tsubame Mizusaki loves to animate, and Sayaka Kanamori knows how to make money. Together, the three start their own animation club at school and get to work bringing their imaginations to life. It is a joyful read for anyone who loves art, storytelling, or creative work.
53: Unnamed Memory by Kuji Furumiya (Yen Press) is a fantasy romance. Prince Oscar has been cursed so that no woman can bear his child, putting his royal line at risk. He travels to the tower of Tinasha, the Witch of the Azure Moon, hoping she can break it, and asks her to marry him instead. She refuses, but agrees to stay with him for a year. It is a lovely pick for readers who like romance between two strong-willed leads.
56: Kingdom Hearts by Shiro Amano (Tokyopop) is a family-friendly adventure based on the video game. Sora, Riku, and Kairi live on the peaceful Destiny Islands, until a dark force swallows their home and scatters them. Sora wakes up in a new world holding a mysterious Keyblade and joins Donald Duck and Goofy on a journey to find his friends. It is a fun read for younger fans of Disney and the games.
57: King's Proposal by Koushi Tachibana (Yen Press) is a fantasy action story. Mushiki Kuga is a boy who is killed, and the world's strongest witch, Saika Kuozaki, is also fatally wounded. To save them both, the two are merged, and Mushiki finds himself living as Saika while trying to protect her secret. It is a quick, playful read for fans of magic school stories.
60: Demon Diary by Lee Chi Hyong and Kara (Tokyopop) is a fantasy comedy from Korea. Raenef is a new demon lord, but he is far too kind and gentle to act the part. His tutor, Eclipse, is a powerful demon determined to teach him how to be truly evil. Their lessons do not go well, and before long a stubborn young priest gets involved too. It is lighthearted and charming, a nice pick for fans of classic fantasy.
61: Wonder Cat Kyuu-chan by Sasami Nitori (Seven Seas) is a cozy, low-key comedy. A man who lives alone takes in a little cat named Kyuu-chan, and life starts to revolve around his new friend. The two settle into a happy rhythm of play, naps, and snacks. It is gentle and short, a sweet read for cat lovers or anyone who needs a calm, smiling break.
63: Samurai Harem: Asu no Yoichi by Yuu Minamoto (Tokyopop) is a romantic comedy. Yoichi Karasuma was raised in the mountains as a samurai, and he has just arrived in the city to train at a dojo. The dojo belongs to four sisters, and they are not quite sure what to make of a young man who acts like he is from another century. It is silly, light, and a nice pick for fans of harem comedy.
64: Dinosaur Sanctuary by Itaru Kinoshita (Seven Seas) is a sci-fi drama set in a world where dinosaurs never went extinct. Suzuka Suma has just started her dream job as a keeper at Enoshima Dinosaur Land. The park is facing hard times, and she has a lot to learn about caring for the animals. It is thoughtful, with real dinosaur science, a great pick for readers who love animals and workplace stories.
66: Scum's Wish by Mengo Yokoyari (Yen Press) is a mature romance and drama. High school students Hanabi and Mugi look like the perfect couple, but each is secretly in love with someone else, two of their teachers. They agree to date as stand-ins for the people they cannot have. It is raw and emotional, best for older readers who like stories about messy, complicated feelings.
67: Seiho Boys' High School! by Kaneyoshi Izumi (Viz Media) is a school comedy and romance. The students at Seiho are stuck at an all-boys school out in the countryside, and most of them would do almost anything to meet a girl. Each one deals with crushes, friendships, and all the awkwardness of being a teenager. It is funny and good-natured, a fun pick for readers who like ensemble comedies.
72: Mahoromatic by Bow Ditama (Tokyopop) is a sci-fi comedy with a bittersweet streak. Mahoro was once a powerful combat android, but now that she has retired, she has chosen to spend her final days as a maid. She goes to work for Suguru Misato, an orphaned boy who lives alone, and the two quickly become part of each other's lives. It mixes goofy comedy with real tenderness, a good pick for fans of classic anime-era manga.
75: Megatokyo by Fred Gallagher (Dark Horse) is a comedy and romance based on the long-running webcomic. Piro and Largo are two American gamers who take a trip to Tokyo, run out of money, and find themselves stranded there. Piro, a shy artist, gets a job at a manga store, while Largo throws himself at every strange situation. It is funny and heartfelt, a fun pick for readers who love otaku culture.
76: Merman in My Tub by Itokichi (Seven Seas) is a laid-back comedy. Tatsumi is an ordinary young man who comes home to find a merman named Wakasa living in his bathtub. Wakasa is demanding, dramatic, and a big fan of video games, and Tatsumi has no idea what to do with him. It is quick, silly fun for readers who like odd-couple comedies.
77: Failure Frame by Kaoru Shinozaki (Seven Seas) is a dark fantasy action story. Touka Mimori is summoned to another world with his entire class, but he is given the lowest possible rank. The goddess who summoned them throws him into a deadly ruin to die. There, Touka discovers his skills are far more dangerous than anyone thought, and he sets out for revenge. It suits readers who like grim, revenge-driven fantasy.
78: First Love Monster by Akira Hiyoshimaru (Yen Press) is a romantic comedy with a strange twist. Kaho Nikaido moves out on her own for high school, and when Kanade Takahashi saves her from an accident, she falls for him on the spot. Kanade is tall and handsome, so it is a shock when she finds out he is actually in fifth grade. It is very silly, and it suits readers who like their comedy over the top.
79: Shonen Note: Boy Soprano by Yuhki Kamatani (Kodansha) is a gentle, quiet drama. Yutaka Aoi is a middle school boy with a beautiful soprano voice who sings in a local choir. He knows his voice will soon change, and he wants to make the most of the time he has left. It is a tender, thoughtful read for anyone who loves music or coming-of-age stories.
80: Silent Möbius by Kia Asamiya (Viz Media) is a sci-fi action series set in a dark future Tokyo. In 2028, the city is under attack from the Lucifer Hawks, creatures from another dimension. A special police unit of women with magical and psychic skills, the AMP, is the only thing standing in their way. It is stylish and atmospheric, a great pick for fans of '90s cyberpunk.
81: Roll Over and Die by Kiki (Seven Seas) is a dark fantasy drama. Flum Apricot is chosen to join the hero's party, but her stats are all zero and no one sees the point of her. One member of the party secretly sells her into slavery, and Flum is left to fight for her own life. It is grim and intense, best for older readers who like underdog stories with dark themes.
82: I Kept Pressing the 100-Million-Year Button and Came Out on Top by Syuichi Tsukishima (Yen Press) is a fantasy action story. Allen Rodol is a struggling student at a swordsmanship academy with no talent at all. A strange man offers him a button that sends him to a dimension where he must spend 100 million years alone. With nothing else to do, Allen spends that time practicing his sword. It is a fun pick for fans of training-arc fantasy.
84: In the Land of Leadale by Ceez (Yen Press) is a gentle fantasy. After years in a hospital bed, Keina Kagami's life support fails, and she wakes up as Cayna, her character from a fantasy game she loved. She discovers the world has moved on 200 years since she last played. It is calm and easygoing, perfect for readers who like slow-paced, slice-of-life isekai.
85: My Friend's Little Sister Has It in for Me! by Mikawaghost (J-Novel Club) is a romantic comedy. Akiteru Oboshi is a practical high school boy who believes romance is a waste of time. That is hard to stick to when his best friend's little sister, Iroha, keeps showing up at his apartment to annoy him. She is cheerful and endlessly teasing, but only around him. It is a fun pick for fans of banter-heavy romance.
87: 7th Time Loop by Minato P (Seven Seas) is a fantasy romance. Rishe has lived her life six times, each time ending in her death at age 20, and she has picked up a lot of skills along the way. On her seventh loop, she meets Arnold Hein, the prince who killed her in a past life, and he asks her to marry him. It is clever and charming, a good pick for fans of villainess stories.
88: Monster Girl Doctor by Yoshino Origuchi (Seven Seas) is a fantasy comedy. Glenn Litbeit is a doctor who runs a clinic in a town where humans and monsters live side by side. With his assistant Sapphee, a lamia, he treats a wide range of monster girls with all sorts of unusual problems. It is light and good-natured, a fun pick for fans of creature-filled fantasy.
90: The World's Finest Assassin Gets Reincarnated in Another World as an Aristocrat by Rui Tsukiyo (Viz Media) is a fantasy action story. The world's best assassin is killed by the organization he served, then offered a second chance by a goddess. He is reborn as Lugh Tuatha Dé, the son of a noble family of assassins, with one task: kill the hero who is fated to destroy the world. It suits readers who like clever, calculating heroes.
91: Slayers by Hajime Kanzaka (CPM) is a fantasy comedy and adventure. Lina Inverse is a teenage sorceress with a big appetite, a short temper, and enough magic to flatten a town. Along with swordsman Gourry Gabriev, she wanders from place to place, looking for treasure and trouble. It is a fun, fast read for fans of classic '90s fantasy.
93: Bofuri: I Don't Want to Get Hurt, So I'll Max Out My Defense by Jirou Oimoto (Yen Press) is a fantasy comedy. Kaede Honjo is new to virtual reality games, and since she hates getting hurt, she puts all her points into defense. Playing as Maple, she turns out to be almost impossible to damage, and she keeps finding strange new skills. It is light, cheerful fun for fans of game stories.
94: Phantom of the Idol by Hijiki Isoflavone (Kodansha) is a supernatural comedy. Yuya Niyodo is a member of the idol group ZINGS, but he has no energy for the job. Then the ghost of a young idol, Asahi Mogami, starts possessing him on stage, and suddenly his performances are amazing. It is a funny, upbeat pick for fans of idol stories.
95: Heaven's Design Team by Hebi-Zou and Tsuta Suzuki (Kodansha) is a workplace comedy with a clever premise. God has decided to create animals for Earth, but has handed the job to a team of designers. Kimura is the new go-between, passing God's requests on to the team and watching them come up with the creatures. It is gentle and funny, with lots of real animal facts.
96: Magus of the Library by Mitsu Izumi (Kodansha) is a fantasy adventure about the love of books. Theo is a poor boy in a small town who is teased for his appearance but loves to read. When he meets a group of kafna, the librarians who protect the great library, he sets his heart on becoming one of them. It is beautifully drawn and a great pick for readers who love books about books.
97: Lucky Star by Kagami Yoshimizu (Bandai) is a laid-back slice-of-life comedy. Konata Izumi is a high school girl who loves anime, manga, and video games far more than studying. She spends her days chatting with her friends, the twins Kagami and Tsukasa and the polite, brainy Miyuki, about snacks, homework, and the little puzzles of everyday life. It is short, low-key fun, a great fit for fans of otaku humor and cozy school comedies.
98: Strobe Edge by Io Sakisaka (Viz Media) is a sweet high school romance and drama. Ninako Kinoshita has never been in love, but everything changes when she gets to know Ren Ichinose, the boy every girl at school is crazy about. Ninako falls for him, but she knows he is already seeing someone else. It is honest and tender, a great pick for fans of classic shojo romance.
99: Saekano: How to Raise a Boring Girlfriend by Fumiaki Maruto (Yen Press) is a romantic comedy. Tomoya Aki is an otaku who wants to make his own dating-sim game. When he meets Megumi Kato, a quiet, plain girl, he decides she will be his heroine. He sets out to build a team of creators, which pulls in a few girls from his past. It is a fun pick for fans of otaku comedy.
100: Kino's Journey: The Beautiful World by Keiichi Sigsawa (Vertical) is a quiet, thoughtful fantasy about travel and the people met along the way. Kino rides from country to country on Hermes, a talking motorcycle, and never stays anywhere longer than three days. Each stop has its own strange customs, kind or cruel, and Kino mostly watches and moves on. It suits readers who like short, reflective stories that leave something to think about.
102: Smoking Behind the Supermarket with You by Jinushi (Square Enix Manga) is a gentle comedy about two tired adults finding a little comfort. Sasaki, a worn-out office worker, looks forward to buying groceries from Yamada, the cheerful cashier at his local supermarket. One night he starts sharing smoke breaks out back with a blunt woman named Tayama, never guessing she is the same cashier out of uniform. It's a sweet, low-key read for grown-ups who like slow-burn romance.
105: Men of the Harem by Alphatart (Ize Press) is a romantic court fantasy full of scheming and politics. Latil becomes the first female emperor of her country, but her throne is shaky and her heart is still bruised from a past love. To win allies and secure her rule, she decides to build a harem of handsome, powerful men. Meanwhile, rumors spread that a legendary dark lord is about to return. It's a great pick for fans of palace intrigue and dramatic romance.
108: Mushishi by Yuki Urushibara (Del Rey) is a calm, atmospheric supernatural story set in a quiet, old-fashioned Japan. Ginko is a mushi master, a wanderer who studies mushi, simple life forms that most people can't see but that can cause strange illnesses and odd happenings. He travels from village to village, helping people whose lives have been touched by them. Each chapter stands mostly on its own, making it a lovely, unhurried read for fans of folklore and quiet mysteries.
110: There's No Freaking Way I'll Be Your Lover! Unless... by Teren Mikami (Seven Seas) is a bubbly yuri romantic comedy. Renako Amaori worked hard to reinvent herself and finally fit in with the popular crowd in high school. Then Mai Oduka, the most dazzling girl in school, confesses to her. Renako insists she only wants to be friends, so Mai makes a bet that she can win her over. It's fun, flustered, and perfect for readers who enjoy silly, sweet romance.
111: Sugar Apple Fairy Tale by Miri Mikawa (Yen Press) is a gentle fantasy romance about chasing a dream. Anne Halford wants to become a silver sugar master, an artist who crafts candy sculptures that carry real meaning in her kingdom. To travel to the royal capital for an important competition, she buys a warrior fairy named Challe to serve as her bodyguard, even though she hates the idea of owning a fairy. It's warm and charming, with a slow-building bond at its heart.
112: I Got Married to the Girl I Hate Most in Class by Amano Seiju (Seven Seas) is a romantic comedy about rivals stuck under one roof. Saito Hojo and Akane Sakuramori are top students who can't stand each other and argue constantly. Then their grandparents arrange for the two of them to marry and live together. Now they have to share a home while keeping it secret from their classmates. It's a light, funny read for fans of bickering couples and slow-warming feelings.
118: The Brilliant Healer's New Life in the Shadows by Sakaku Hishikawa (J-Novel Club) is a fantasy light novel with a big heart and a dry sense of humor. Zenos grew up in the slums and taught himself healing magic, but his adventuring party kicks him out for being too low-born. Rather than give up, he opens an unlicensed clinic in the slums, where his skills turn out to be far greater than anyone guessed. It's a cozy underdog story for readers who like found-family fantasy.
122: Issak by Shinji Makari and Double-S (Kodansha) is a gritty historical action story set in 17th-century Europe. During the Thirty Years' War, a quiet Japanese mercenary arrives in Germany carrying a matchlock rifle of remarkable accuracy. Known as Issak, he joins the fighting while hunting a man he has followed across the world. It's a tense, well-researched read for fans of war stories, sharpshooters, and samurai tales told far from home.
125: The Climber by Shin-ichi Sakamoto (Seven Seas) is an intense, beautifully drawn drama about one young man and the mountains. Buntaro Mori is a lonely, withdrawn transfer student until a classmate dares him to climb the outside of their school building. That climb awakens something in him, and he begins pushing himself toward harder and more dangerous ascents. Based on a novel by Jiro Nitta, it's a striking pick for readers who like serious, character-driven sports stories.
126: Ossan Idol! by Mochiko Mochida (Tokyopop) is a cheerful comedy about starting over in middle age. Nobuo Mineyama is a 40-something office worker who decides it's time to get in shape. When videos of his workouts and dancing start getting attention online, he finds himself on an unlikely path toward becoming an idol. It's an upbeat, feel-good read for anyone who likes stories about chasing something new at any age.
129: Flowers and Bees by Moyoco Anno (Viz Media) is a sharp, silly comedy about wanting to be cool. Masao Komatsu is an awkward high school boy desperate to become attractive and finally get a girlfriend. He wanders into a men's beauty salon run by two glamorous, merciless sisters, who take him on as their latest project. What follows is a string of humiliating makeovers. It's a fun read for fans of over-the-top teen comedy.
132: Absolute Boyfriend by Yuu Watase (Viz Media) is a romantic comedy with a sci-fi twist. Riiko Izawa has terrible luck with boys, so when she stumbles onto a website selling the perfect boyfriend, she gives it a try. A box soon arrives with Night, a lifelike robot designed to love her completely. Then comes the bill for the trial, and it's far more than she can pay. It's a playful, heartfelt read for longtime shojo fans.
133: Aishiteruze Baby by Yoko Maki (Viz Media) is a sweet, funny shojo story about growing up by taking care of someone else. Kippei Katakura is a carefree high school flirt with no interest in responsibility. Then his five-year-old cousin Yuzuyu comes to live with his family after her mother leaves, and Kippei is put in charge of looking after her. It's tender and warmhearted, a good pick for readers who love family stories with a light touch.
135: Monster Musume by OKAYADO (Seven Seas) is a goofy, fan-service-heavy comedy for older teens and adults. Kimihito Kurusu is an ordinary young man who ends up as a host family under a government program that brings mythical species into human society. His first guest is Miia, a lamia who is half woman and half snake, and more monster girls soon move in. It's a light, cheeky read for fans of harem comedy.
138: That Wolf-Boy Is Mine! by Yoko Nogiri (Kodansha) is a light shojo romance with a supernatural twist. Komugi Inugami has just transferred to a new high school in Hokkaido and is hoping to make friends. She's drawn to her quiet classmate Yu Sakuraba, then discovers his secret: he can turn into a wolf. Soon she learns he isn't the only shapeshifter at school. It's a cute, cozy series for readers who like gentle romance and fluffy animal charm.
140: The All-New Tenchi Muyo! by Hitoshi Okuda (Viz Media) is a lighthearted sci-fi comedy based on the long-running anime. Tenchi Masaki is a regular teenager whose quiet country home has been overrun by alien women, including the wild space pirate Ryoko and the proud princess Ayeka. Between rivalries, space visitors, and household chaos, Tenchi rarely gets a moment's peace. It's a fun pick for fans of the anime and classic harem comedy.
141: Angelic Layer by CLAMP (Tokyopop) is a bright, energetic action story about a game and the friends made through it. Misaki Suzuhara moves to Tokyo and discovers Angelic Layer, a popular game where players control small dolls called Angels with their minds and battle in an arena. Small for her age but full of spirit, Misaki builds her own Angel, Hikaru, and jumps into competition. It's a lively read for fans of tournament stories and CLAMP's art.
144: My Status as an Assassin Obviously Exceeds the Hero's by Matsuri Akai (Seven Seas) is a darker take on the summoned-to-another-world fantasy. Akira Oda is a quiet student who gets transported to a fantasy kingdom along with his entire class. Assigned the class of Assassin, he finds his stats are far stronger than those of the classmate named the Hero. When Akira learns the kingdom isn't what it seems, he slips into the shadows to uncover the truth. It suits fans of isekai with an edge.
146: Aria by Kozue Amano (ADV) is a peaceful, slice-of-life science fiction story set on a future Mars covered in water. In the city of Neo-Venezia, Akari Mizunashi is training to become an Undine, a gondolier who guides tourists through the canals. Each chapter follows her small adventures, new friendships, and quiet discoveries around town. It's a soothing, gently beautiful read for anyone who wants a calm, comforting story.
147: Negima!? Neo by Ken Akamatsu (Kodansha) is a lively magical comedy that reimagines the world of Negima! Magister Negi Magi. Negi Springfield is a ten-year-old wizard sent to Japan to teach a class of rowdy middle school girls, all while keeping his magic a secret. This spin-off retells his adventures with a lighter, sillier spin. It's a fun extra for fans of the original series and its huge cast.
148: Attack on Titan Colossal Edition by Hajime Isayama (Kodansha) collects the dark fantasy action series in oversized omnibus volumes. Humanity survives behind enormous walls, hiding from Titans, giant humanlike creatures that devour people. When a colossal Titan breaks through the wall of his hometown, young Eren Yeager vows to fight back. It's tense, grim, and gripping, and these big editions are a great way for fans to own or revisit the series.
149: The Faraway Paladin Omnibus by Kanata Yanagino (J-Novel Club) is a warm, thoughtful fantasy about family and second chances. After an unhappy life, a young man is reborn in a world of swords and magic as a baby named Will. He is raised in a ruined city by three undead guardians: a skeleton warrior, a mummified priestess, and a ghostly sorcerer. As Will grows, he begins to wonder why they're there. It's a heartfelt read for fans of classic fantasy adventure.
152: The Good Witch of the West by Noriko Ogiwara and Haruhiko Momokawa (Tokyopop) is a romantic fantasy with court intrigue. Firiel Dee is a cheerful country girl and the daughter of a reclusive astronomer. On her fifteenth birthday she receives her late mother's necklace, and wearing it to her first ball reveals that she may be in line for the throne. Suddenly she's caught up in royal politics and danger. It's a fun read for fans of classic shojo fantasy.
153: Hetalia: Axis Powers by Hidekaz Himaruya (Tokyopop) is a goofy comedy that turns world history into a cast of quirky characters. Each country is a person: Italy is a cheerful, pasta-loving slacker, Germany is his stern and serious friend, and Japan is polite and reserved. Their short, silly adventures poke fun at national stereotypes and real historical events. It's a quick, playful read for history buffs and anyone who likes gag comedy.
154: The Hero Is Overpowered but Overly Cautious by Light Tuchihi (Yen Press) is a fantasy comedy that pokes fun at the usual hero story. The goddess Ristarte summons Seiya Ryuguin to save a very dangerous world, and he turns out to be incredibly strong. The trouble is that he's also incredibly cautious, insisting on endless training and preparing for every possible threat, no matter how small. It's a funny, fast read for fans of isekai parody.
161: Orc Eroica by Rifujin na Magonote (Yen Press) is a fantasy comedy light novel with a surprisingly earnest hero. Bash is the greatest warrior the orcs have ever known, a hero of the recent war. In orc society, though, being a virgin is a mark of shame, and Bash has never had a partner. Now that peace has come, he sets out to find a wife, honorably, which proves harder than any battle. It's a goofy, good-natured read from the author of Mushoku Tensei.
169: The Seven Deadly Sins Omnibus by Nakaba Suzuki (Kodansha) collects the action fantasy series in larger, value-packed volumes. The Seven Deadly Sins were once a band of legendary knights, until they were accused of treason and scattered. Princess Elizabeth sets out to find them to save her kingdom and stumbles into a tavern run by Meliodas, a cheerful young man with a talking pig. It's fun, fast-moving adventure for shonen fans.
171: Idol Dreams by Arina Tanemura (Viz Media) is a romantic drama about getting a second chance at youth. Chikage Ichinose is a 31-year-old office worker who feels she missed out on love and fun as a teenager. When a mysterious pill makes her look fifteen again, she seizes the chance and ends up stepping into the world of idols. It's sweet, a bit bittersweet, and great for readers who like grown-up heroines.
173: The Tarot Cafe by Sang-Sun Park (Tokyopop) is a dark, dreamy fantasy manhwa told through supernatural stories. Pamela runs a small tarot shop, and her most important clients come at night: werewolves, fairies, witches, and other creatures seeking answers. Each reading reveals a story of love, loss, or regret, while Pamela keeps a long-held secret of her own. It's a moody, gothic read for fans of folklore and beautiful art.
174: Peacemaker Kurogane by Nanae Chrono (Tokyopop) is a historical action story set in the final years of the samurai. Tetsunosuke Ichimura is a short-tempered teen who wants revenge for the murder of his parents. Hoping to become strong, he joins the Shinsengumi, the famous police force of Kyoto, where he finds both friendship and danger. It's a lively blend of humor and drama for fans of samurai stories.
175: Imadoki! by Yuu Watase (Viz Media) is a gentle shojo comedy about staying true to yourself. Tanpopo Yamazaki moves from the countryside to attend Meio Academy, an elite school full of rich kids who mostly ignore her. Determined to make friends, she decides to start a gardening committee, and along the way she gets to know Koki, a boy who isn't quite what he seems. It's a sweet, upbeat read about kindness and growing roots.
177: Brave Story by Miyuki Miyabe (Viz Media) is a heartfelt fantasy adventure about a boy facing hard times. Eleven-year-old Wataru Mitani's ordinary life falls apart when his family is torn apart. When a mysterious door opens into a magical world called Vision, Wataru learns that whoever completes a quest there may change their fate. He sets out on a journey full of danger and new friends. It's a strong pick for fans of classic quest stories.
180: In the Land of Leadale by Ceez (Yen Press) is a cozy fantasy about waking up in a game world. After a long illness, Keina passes away and wakes up as Cayna, her high elf character from the VR game she loved. The world looks like Leadale, but two hundred years have passed, and her old friends and creations have changed. It's a relaxing, gentle isekai for readers who prefer exploration and found family to big battles.
182: Candy Color Paradox by Isaku Natsume (SuBLime) is a lively boys' love romance set in the world of tabloid journalism. Onoe is a hardworking reporter who gets transferred to a gossip magazine and paired with Kaburagi, a skilled but cocky photographer. The two clash constantly as they stake out celebrity scandals, but long nights together start to change things. It's a fun, funny pick for fans of rivals-to-lovers BL.
184: Irina: The Vampire Cosmonaut by Keisuke Makino (Seven Seas) is a sci-fi romance light novel set during an alternate Cold War space race. Lev Leps is a cosmonaut candidate in a nation desperate to reach space first. He is assigned to supervise Irina Luminesk, a vampire chosen as a test subject to be sent into orbit before any human. It's a touching, slow-burn story for readers who like romance mixed with history and science.
187: Chitose Is in the Ramune Bottle by Hiromu (Yen Press) is a high school romance and drama with a popular kid at its center. Saku Chitose is at the top of his school's social ladder, handsome, confident, and surrounded by friends. One day his teacher asks him to help Kenta, a shut-in classmate, return to school. Saku takes on the job in his own way. It's a thoughtful read for fans of character-driven school stories.
192: Combatants Will Be Dispatched! by Natsume Akatsuki (Yen Press) is a sci-fi comedy light novel from the creator of KonoSuba. Combatant Agent Six works for the Kisaragi Corporation, an evil secret organization bent on world domination. He is sent to an alien planet to scout it for invasion, along with a high-tech android partner. Once there, he gets caught up in a fantasy kingdom's war. It's silly, rowdy fun for fans of comedy that doesn't take itself seriously.
197: Ran and the Gray World by Aki Irie (Viz Media) is a whimsical, beautifully drawn fantasy about growing up. Ran Uruma is a ten-year-old girl from a family of magic users, and she can't wait to be an adult. By slipping on her mother's magic sneakers, she can turn into a grown woman for a while, though she's still a kid inside. It's a charming, imaginative read for fans of gentle magical stories.
200: Kashimashi: Girl Meets Girl by Satoru Akahori and Yukimaru Katsura (Seven Seas) is a gentle romantic comedy with a sci-fi twist. Hazumu Osaragi is a shy, kind boy who has just been turned down by his crush, Yasuna. Then an alien spaceship crashes on him, and he wakes up as a girl. Now Hazumu has to relearn daily life while caught between Yasuna and his tomboyish childhood friend Tomari. It's a sweet, funny pick for fans of yuri and love triangles.
203: Record of Grancrest War by Ryo Mizuno and Makoto Yotsuba (Viz Media) is a fantasy war story full of knights, mages and shifting alliances. The continent is torn by Chaos, and the lords who hold the power to calm it are too busy fighting each other. Siluca Meletes, a gifted mage, makes a contract with Theo Cornaro, a wandering knight with a small Crest and a big dream of freeing his homeland. Readers who like strategy and political fantasy will feel at home here.
205: Kyo Kara Maoh! by Tomo Takabayashi and Temari Matsumoto (Tokyopop) is a lighthearted fantasy comedy. Yuri Shibuya is an ordinary, baseball-loving high schooler until a pack of bullies dunks his head in a toilet and he gets flushed into another world. There he learns he is the new Demon King, expected to rule a kingdom he knows nothing about. Readers who enjoy fish-out-of-water humor and a big cast of handsome retainers will have fun with it.
208: Saikano by Shin Takahashi (Viz Media) is a bittersweet sci-fi romance. Shuji and Chise are high school classmates in a small seaside town, awkwardly figuring out how to be a couple. Then a sudden air raid reveals that clumsy, shy Chise has been turned into the military's ultimate weapon. The story follows two teens trying to hold on to an ordinary love while the world falls into war. It's a good fit for readers who like tender, melancholy stories.
211: Sakura Taisen by Ohji Hiroi and Ikku Masa (Tokyopop) is an action story set in a steam-powered version of 1920s Tokyo. Navy officer Ichiro Ogami expects a combat command, but he's assigned to the Imperial Floral Assault Troupe, a group of young women who perform as a theater company. Secretly, they also pilot steam-driven mecha to defend the city from demons. Fans of the classic Sega games will enjoy seeing the cast on the page.
213: Scott Pilgrim by Bryan Lee O'Malley (Oni Press) is a funny, energetic comic about love, music and video games. Scott is a 23-year-old slacker in Toronto who plays bass in a struggling band. When he falls for Ramona Flowers, a mysterious delivery girl, he learns that to date her, he has to defeat her seven evil exes in battle. It's a great pick for anyone who grew up on video games and indie rock.
216: Love Stage!! by Eiki Eiki and Taishi Zaou (Sublime) is a bright, silly boys' love romantic comedy. Izumi Sena comes from a famous showbiz family, but all he wants is to be a manga artist and enjoy his anime. Years ago he played a bride in a TV commercial, and when the crew reunites for a sequel, rising actor Ryoma learns that the girl he has been pining for is actually a boy. Fans of lighthearted BL will find plenty to laugh at.
217: Dragon Quest: The Adventure of Dai by Riku Sanjo and Koji Inada (Viz Media) is a classic fantasy adventure. Dai is a boy raised by friendly monsters on a remote island, and he dreams of becoming a great hero. When the Dark King Hadlar returns and the island's monsters turn wild, Dai sets out to train and fight with a growing band of friends. It's a warm, exciting read for fans of the games and old-school shonen action.
220: Mamotte! Lollipop by Michiyo Kikuta (Kodansha) is a cute, bubbly magical romance. Nina is a middle schooler who accidentally swallows the Crystal Pearl, a prize that wizards-in-training need to pass their exam. Suddenly she's a target, and two young wizards, Zero and Ichii, step in to protect her while trying to get the pearl back. It's a fun, light pick for younger shojo readers who like magic and cute boys.
222: Durarara!! by Ryohgo Narita and Akiyo Satorigi (Yen Press) is a stylish urban mystery with a supernatural edge. Mikado Ryugamine moves to Tokyo's Ikebukuro district hoping for a more exciting life. He quickly finds it, along with color gangs, a vending-machine-throwing strongman, an information broker and the city's most famous urban legend: a headless rider on a black motorcycle. Readers who like large casts and interlocking stories will enjoy this one.
223: Fake by Sanami Matoh (Tokyopop) is a boys' love police drama with plenty of humor. Randy "Ryo" MacLean is a new detective at New York's 27th Precinct, and he is partnered with Dee Laytner, a brash cop who makes his interest in Ryo very clear. Between murder cases and street crime, the two slowly figure out what they mean to each other. It's a classic BL series that fans of buddy-cop stories will enjoy.
224: Fighting for Tomorrow (Ashita no Joe) by Asao Takamori and Tetsuya Chiba (Kodansha) is a gritty, classic boxing drama. Joe Yabuki is a reckless young drifter who wanders into Tokyo's slums looking for trouble. Danpei Tange, a washed-up former boxer, sees raw talent in him and is determined to turn him into a champion, if Joe can stay out of trouble long enough. It's a landmark sports manga for anyone who loves underdog stories.
225: Sherlock Bones by Yuma Ando and Yuki Sato (Kodansha) is a lighthearted mystery comedy. High schooler Takeru Wajo adopts a puppy, and soon learns that it's the reincarnation of Sherlock Holmes himself. Takeru is the only one who can understand him, so the pair work together to help Takeru's detective father crack his cases, with Takeru taking the credit. It's a fun, quick read for fans of whodunits and goofy animal sidekicks.
227: Shoulder-a-Coffin Kuro by Satoko Kiyuduki (Yen Press) is a quiet, dreamlike fantasy. Kuro is a traveler dressed all in black who carries a coffin on her back wherever she goes. With her talking bat companion Sen, she wanders from town to town in search of the witch who cursed her, meeting strange and kind people along the way. It's a gentle, melancholy story for readers who like fairy-tale moods and soft art.
229: Yu-Gi-Oh! Millennium World by Kazuki Takahashi (Viz Media) is the action-adventure final arc of the original Yu-Gi-Oh! story. Yugi Mutou and the spirit of the nameless Pharaoh who lives inside the Millennium Puzzle have gathered the clues they need to uncover the Pharaoh's lost past. The journey takes them into his memories of ancient Egypt, where monster battles are real. Fans of the original series will want this to finish the story.
230: Full Moon O Sagashite by Arina Tanemura (Viz Media) is an emotional shojo fantasy about music and dreams. Twelve-year-old Mitsuki Koyama wants to be a singer, but a tumor in her throat stands in her way. Then two shinigami appear to her, and one of them gives her the power to transform into a healthy sixteen-year-old so she can chase her dream. It's a heartfelt read for fans of magical girls and bittersweet romance.
232: The Executioner and Her Way of Life by Mato Sato and Ryo Mitsuya (Yen Press) is a dark fantasy with a twist on isekai stories. In this world, people summoned from Japan arrive with dangerous powers, and Menou is the executioner sent to quietly kill them. Her newest target, the cheerful Akari, turns out to be far harder to get rid of than any before. Readers who like yuri, assassins and morally gray heroines will enjoy it.
233: Black Bullet by Shiden Kanzaki with illustrations by Saki Ukai (Yen Press) is a sci-fi action light novel series. Humanity survives behind walls that keep out the Gastrea, monsters created by a parasitic virus. Rentaro Satomi is a young Civil Security officer who fights them alongside his partner, Enju, one of the Cursed Children, girls born with powers from the virus. It's a fast, hard-hitting read for fans of dystopian battle stories.
236: Days with My Stepsister by Ghost Mikawa (Seven Seas) is a quiet, grounded romance light novel. When high schooler Yuta Asamura's father remarries, Yuta gains a stepsister his own age, the cool and guarded Saki Ayase. The two agree not to expect too much from each other and to keep things honest, but sharing a home slowly changes how they see one another. It's a thoughtful slow burn for readers who prefer realistic, low-drama romance.
237: Solo Leveling by Chugong (Yen Press) is the original Korean web novel behind the hit action series. Monsters pour into the world through dungeon gates, and hunters with special powers fight them. Sung Jinwoo is known as the world's weakest hunter, until a deadly raid leaves him with a mysterious System that lets him level up like a game character. Fans of the manhwa and anime will enjoy reading the story in its first form.
238: Bungo Stray Dogs by Kafka Asagiri (Yen Press) is a set of light novels that expand on the supernatural detective series. The main story follows Atsushi Nakajima, an orphan who joins the Armed Detective Agency, a team of gifted people named after famous authors. The novels fill in side stories and backstories for the cast, including Dazai's early days. They're a great pick for fans of the manga and anime who want more of these characters.
239: Fullmetal Alchemist by Makoto Inoue (Viz Media) is a series of light novels based on Hiromu Arakawa's fantasy adventure manga. Brothers Edward and Alphonse Elric tried to use alchemy to bring back their mother and paid a terrible price. Now they travel the country searching for the Philosopher's Stone to restore their bodies. These novels tell new standalone adventures from that journey, so they're a nice extra for fans who've finished the manga.
240: Re:ZERO -Starting Life in Another World- by Tappei Nagatsuki (Yen Press) is a dark fantasy manga adaptation of the hit light novels. Subaru Natsuki is a shut-in who is suddenly pulled into a fantasy world with no powers at all. He soon learns he has one strange ability: when he dies, time rewinds to an earlier point. He uses it to protect Emilia, the silver-haired girl who helped him. Readers who like tense, emotional isekai will be hooked.
241: Naruto by Masashi Kishimoto (Viz Media) has a set of light novels that add new stories to the beloved ninja series. Naruto Uzumaki is a loud, lonely orphan in the Hidden Leaf Village who dreams of becoming Hokage, the village's strongest ninja. The novels give side characters and later chapters of the Naruto world more room to breathe. They're a nice extra for fans who want more after finishing the manga.
243: Haruka: Beyond the Stream of Time by Tohko Mizuno (Viz Media) is a historical fantasy romance. High schooler Akane Motomiya is pulled into Kyo, a world modeled on Heian-era Japan. There she learns she is the Priestess of the Dragon God, the one person who can save the capital from a demon clan. Eight handsome guardians are sworn to protect her as she learns her new role. Fans of reverse-harem fantasy will enjoy the setting.
245: Tokyo ESP by Hajime Segawa (Vertical) is a superpowered action story set in Tokyo. Rinka Urushiba is a poor but kind high school girl who lives with her father. One night she sees a glowing flying fish, and the next morning she can pass through solid objects. Soon people all over the city are gaining powers, and Rinka must decide what kind of hero she wants to be. It's a fun pick for fans of action with a strong heroine.
246: Mr. Villain's Day Off by Yuu Morikawa (Square Enix Manga) is a cozy slice-of-life comedy. The General is a fearsome commander in an evil organization fighting the local superhero team. On his days off, though, he's a polite guy who loves pandas, tries new snacks and gets flustered by small kindnesses. The humor comes from the gap between his job and his gentle hobbies. It's a sweet, relaxing read for anyone who wants a smile.
247: Night of the Living Cat by Hawkman and Mecha-Roots (Seven Seas) is a goofy horror comedy. A strange plague has spread across the world: anyone who touches a cat turns into one. Society has collapsed into a fluffy apocalypse, and the few remaining humans must resist the urge to pet, cuddle or feed the cats around them. It's a perfect pick for cat lovers and anyone who enjoys a zombie story played for laughs.
248: Dogs: Bullets & Carnage by Shirow Miwa (Viz Media) is a stylish, violent action series. In a decaying city above a mysterious underground, four very different people make their living with blades and bullets: a retired hitman, a chain-smoking freelancer, a scarred gunman and a young swordswoman searching for the man who killed her mother. Their paths slowly cross. It's a great fit for readers who like gritty, cinematic art and antiheroes.
251: Yuzu the Pet Vet by Mingo Ito (Kodansha) is a warm, kid-friendly story about caring for animals. Yuzu is an elementary school girl who loves animals and spends her time at her uncle's veterinary clinic. Each chapter brings new pets and owners with problems to solve, and Yuzu learns more about what it takes to be a vet. It's a great pick for young readers, with real tips on pet care tucked into the stories.
253: Classmates by Asumiko Nakamura (Seven Seas) is a gentle boys' love romance. Hikaru Kusakabe plays guitar in a band, and Rihito Sajo is the top student in their class. When Hikaru offers to help Rihito practice for the school chorus festival, the two boys slowly become close and fall in love. The story is soft, quiet and full of small moments. It's a lovely pick for readers who want a sweet, low-key high school romance.
256: Saturn Apartments by Hisae Iwaoka (Viz Media) is a gentle sci-fi slice-of-life story. In the far future, humanity lives in a giant ring that circles the Earth, with the rich on the upper levels and the working class below. Mitsu takes up his late father's job as a window washer on the ring's outer wall. Each chapter follows the people he meets through the glass. It's a calm, thoughtful read for fans of quiet, everyday stories.
257: From the New World by Yusuke Kishi and Toru Oikawa (Vertical) is a sci-fi mystery set a thousand years in the future. Saki Watanabe grows up in Kamisu 66, a peaceful village where people have psychokinetic powers. As she and her friends start learning to use their abilities, they begin to notice that their perfect world is hiding some very dark secrets. Readers who like dystopian mysteries with a slow-building sense of dread will enjoy it.
259: Grenadier by Sousuke Kaise (Tokyopop) is a lighthearted action story with a gentle heroine. Rushuna Tendou is a wandering gunslinger in a world at war, but she would rather end a fight with a smile than a bullet. Her goal is to disarm her enemies and win them over with kindness. Along the way she travels with Yajiro, a serious young swordsman. It's a good fit for readers who like western-style action with a soft heart.
260: Forbidden Scrollery by ZUN and Moe Harukawa (Yen Press) is a cozy fantasy story set in the Touhou Project world of Gensokyo. Kosuzu Motoori is a curious girl who works at her family's book rental shop in the human village. She can read any writing, including the dangerous youkai books that come through the shop, and her curiosity keeps getting her into trouble. It's a charming pick for Touhou fans and anyone who loves book-themed stories.
262: Associate Professor Akira Takatsuki's Conjecture by Mikage Sawamura (Yen Press) is a gentle mystery light novel. Naoya Fukamachi is a college student who can hear lies, which has made him lonely. He signs up for a folklore class taught by the charming Akira Takatsuki and ends up as the professor's assistant, helping him look into urban legends and strange incidents. Readers who like low-key mysteries and odd-couple partners will enjoy it.
264: Inside Mari by Shuzo Oshimi (Denpa) is a psychological drama about identity. Isao is a lonely college dropout who spends his days gaming and secretly following a high school girl named Mari on her way home. One morning he wakes up in Mari's body, with no idea where Mari herself has gone. The story is tense, strange and thoughtful about how people see themselves. It's for older readers who like unsettling, character-driven stories.
267: Pretty Guardian Sailor Moon Eternal Edition by Naoko Takeuchi (Kodansha) is the classic magical-girl story in a larger, deluxe format. Usagi Tsukino is a crybaby middle schooler until she meets Luna, a talking cat who tells her she is the warrior Sailor Moon. Soon Usagi is fighting evil and gathering the other Sailor Guardians. It's a wonderful way for longtime fans and new readers to enjoy the series with better paper and color pages.
269: Goodnight Punpun by Inio Asano (Viz Media) is a raw, emotional coming-of-age drama. Punpun Onodera is an ordinary boy, though he's drawn as a simple cartoon bird, and the story follows him from childhood into adulthood. It begins as he falls for Aiko, a new girl at school, while his family falls apart around him. It's a moving, often heavy read for older readers who appreciate honest and experimental storytelling.
270: The Kurosagi Corpse Delivery Service by Eiji Otsuka and Housui Yamazaki (Dark Horse) is a darkly funny horror mystery. Five students at a Buddhist university can't find jobs, so they start a business using their odd talents. Kuro Karatsu can talk to the dead, and the team helps corpses finish their business, whether that means getting home or getting revenge. It's a great pick for readers who like horror mixed with humor.
275: Agents of the Four Seasons by Kana Akatsuki (Yen Press) is a beautiful fantasy light novel from the author of Violet Evergarden. In this world, the seasons are brought each year by four chosen Agents. Hinagiku, the Agent of Spring, returns after being missing for ten years, and with her loyal guard Sakura, she sets out to bring spring back to the land. It's a lyrical, emotional read for fans of gentle fantasy and strong bonds.
279: The Shiunji Family Children by Reiji Miyajima (Yen Press) is a romantic comedy about a big, unusual family. Arata Shiunji has grown up as the only son among six sisters in a wealthy household. One day their father reveals that none of the siblings are related by blood, and suddenly everyone in the house sees each other differently. Fans of family comedy and harem romance will enjoy the chaos.
280: Alive: The Final Evolution by Tadashi Kawashima and Adachitoka (Del Rey) is a sci-fi thriller. A strange wave of suicides sweeps across the world, and the few survivors who resist it come away changed, with new powers. Taisuke Kanou is an ordinary high schooler whose friends are caught up in the outbreak, and he finds himself pulled into a fight to understand what's happening. It's a tense read for fans of dark sci-fi.
282: Cosmos by Ryuhei Tamura (Viz Media) is a supernatural mystery with action. Kanade Mizuhara is a young man who can tell when people are lying, a gift that has made his life hard. He's recruited by Cosmos, an insurance investigation company that looks into fraud involving aliens living secretly among humans. It's a fun pick for readers who like quirky investigators and monster-of-the-week cases.
287: The World's Strongest Rearguard: Labyrinth Country's Novice Seeker by Tôwa with illustrations by Huuka Kazabana (Yen Press) is a fantasy adventure light novel. Office worker Arihito Atobe dies in a bus accident and wakes in a world of labyrinths. He's given the job of Rearguard, a support class that powers up allies from behind, and he forms a party with his former boss. Fans of party-building dungeon stories will enjoy it.
289: Rozen Maiden by PEACH-PIT (Seven Seas) is a gothic fantasy drama. Jun Sakurada is a middle schooler who has shut himself in his room. One day he receives a mysterious box containing Shinku, a beautiful living doll who demands he become her servant. Soon Jun is pulled into the Alice Game, a battle between living dolls who all want to become the perfect girl. Fans of gothic fashion and dark fairy tales will love it.
295: Übel Blatt by Etorouji Shiono (Yen Press) is a dark fantasy story of revenge. Years ago, fourteen young warriors were sent to stop an invasion, and the survivors were hailed as the Seven Heroes. Now a young-looking swordsman named Köinzell travels the empire, hunting those heroes with a deadly purpose of his own. It's a grim, action-heavy series for older readers who like brutal battles and political fantasy.
296: Classroom for Heroes by Shin Araki (Yen Press) is a fantasy school comedy light novel. Blade is the hero who defeated the Demon Lord, but he has no idea how to live a normal life. To learn, he enrolls at Rostalgia Academy as an ordinary student, where his overwhelming strength and total lack of common sense cause constant trouble. It's a light, fun read for readers who enjoy overpowered heroes and school antics.
298: Gods' Games We Play by Kei Sazane (Yen Press) is a fantasy light novel about high-stakes games. In this world, the gods are bored, and they challenge humans to games of wit and strategy. Fay is a young apostle with a talent for these contests, and he teams up with Leshea, a former goddess who wants to play for herself. Readers who like clever puzzles and battles of wits will have fun with it.
301: Kaya-chan Isn't Scary by Yuritaro (Seven Seas) is a horror comedy with a tough little heroine. Chie is a kindergarten teacher who keeps noticing that one of her students, the stone-faced Kaya, reacts to things no one else can see. Kaya can see evil spirits, and she deals with them by fighting back. It's a fun pick for readers who like spooky stories with a big helping of laughs.
305: The Fox and Little Tanuki by Mi Tagawa (Tokyopop) is a gentle fantasy about growing up. Senzou, a powerful black fox spirit, has been locked away for misbehaving. To earn his freedom, the Sun Goddess makes him mentor Manpachi, a small and very eager tanuki who wants to serve the gods. The grumpy fox and the cheerful little tanuki make a sweet pair, and it's a great choice for younger readers and families.
306: Animal Crossing by Kokonasu Rumba (Viz Media) is a lighthearted comedy based on the Nintendo game. The story follows a new arrival who moves to a deserted island and starts building a life there with a cast of animal neighbors. Each chapter brings small adventures, silly misunderstandings, and island projects. It's a cheerful, easy read for kids and for any fan of the games who wants more time on the island.
308: Raven of the Inner Palace by Kouko Shirakawa (Seven Seas) is a historical fantasy mystery light novel. Deep inside the emperor's inner palace lives the Raven Consort, a woman who never visits the emperor and is rumored to have strange powers. When the young emperor Gao Jun comes to her with a request, she is pulled into secrets she would rather avoid. It's a quiet, atmospheric read for fans of court intrigue and ghostly mysteries.
309: Ninja Slayer by Bradley Bond (Vertical) is a cyberpunk action story with a wild sense of style. In the neon city of Neo-Saitama, an ordinary salaryman loses his wife and son when they are caught in a battle between ninja. Dying, he is possessed by a vengeful ninja soul and rises as Ninja Slayer, sworn to kill every ninja he can find. It's fast, violent, and deliberately over the top, made for readers who enjoy bold action.
310: Nausicaä of the Valley of the Wind by Hayao Miyazaki (Viz Media) is a sweeping fantasy set long after a war that wrecked the world. A toxic jungle filled with giant insects is spreading across the land, and Nausicaä, the young princess of a small valley, studies it while others fear it. When war comes to her people, she is drawn into the conflict. It's a thoughtful, beautifully drawn story that goes much deeper than the film.
311: Aria The Masterpiece by Kozue Amano (Dark Horse) is a calm, gentle slice-of-life story. On a terraformed Mars now called Aqua, the city of Neo-Venezia is famous for its canals. Akari Mizunashi arrives there to train as an Undine, a gondolier who guides tourists through the city. Each chapter follows her small discoveries and friendships, making it a soothing read for anyone who enjoys cozy, low-stakes stories.
313: A Galaxy Next Door by Gido Amagakure (Kodansha) is a sweet romantic comedy. Ichiro Kuga is a young manga artist working hard to support his little brother and sister. When he needs an assistant, he hires Shiori Goshiki, a calm and lovely young woman who turns out to have a very unusual secret. It's a warm story about family and first love, perfect for readers who like gentle romance.
314: A Polar Bear in Love by Koromo (Yen Press) is a cute comedy romance. A polar bear meets a little seal and falls head over heels in love at first sight. The seal, though, is sure the bear is just trying to eat him and spends every moment terrified. The misunderstandings keep piling up in short, funny chapters, making this a sweet pick for animal lovers and fans of light comedy.
315: A Returner's Magic Should Be Special by Wookjakga (Yen Press) is a fantasy action manhwa. Desir Arman is one of the last survivors fighting the Shadow Labyrinth, a disaster that destroys the world. When he fails, he wakes up thirteen years in the past, just as he is about to enter magic school. He sets out to use what he knows to change the future. It's a good fit for fans of time-loop stories and magic academy adventures.
316: Spy Classroom by Takemachi (Yen Press) is a spy action comedy. Klaus, a brilliant spy, is put in charge of a team for a mission so dangerous it is called impossible. The catch is that his team is made up of seven girls who all flunked out of spy school, and Klaus is a terrible teacher. Lots of twists and teamwork make it a fun read for fans of heist and spy stories.
318: Mink by Megumi Tachikawa (Tokyopop) is a bubbly sci-fi comedy. Mink is an ordinary middle school girl who dreams of becoming a famous idol. When she gets her hands on a strange gadget from the future, she can transform into a glamorous cyber idol. Keeping her double life a secret turns out to be harder than she expected. It's a light, fun read for fans of magical girl and idol stories.
320: Gannibal by Masaaki Ninomiya (Ablaze Manga) is a tense horror thriller. Police officer Daigo Agawa transfers to Kuge, a remote mountain village, with his wife and young daughter. The villagers seem friendly, but Daigo soon hears rumors that the powerful family who controls the area eats people. As he digs deeper, the village grows more threatening. It's a slow-burn, unsettling read for fans of dark mysteries and rural horror.
325: Girls' Last Tour by Tsukumizu (Yen Press) is a quiet sci-fi story set at the end of the world. Chito and Yuuri are two girls traveling through the ruins of an empty city on a small tracked vehicle, searching for food, fuel, and whatever is left. They have little but each other, but they find small joys along the way. It's gentle, thoughtful, and a little melancholy, perfect for readers who enjoy reflective stories.
326: Gokurakugai by Yuto Sano (Viz Media) is a stylish supernatural action story. In Gokurakugai, a rough walled-off part of town, Tao and Alma run a troubleshooting office that will take almost any job. Many of those jobs involve the Magai, monsters that prey on people. Sharp art, a lively setting, and an easygoing partnership make this a strong pick for fans of demon-hunting action series.
327: Gold Digger by Fred Perry (Antarctic Press) is a fun action adventure comic with a manga style. Gina Diggers is a genius scientist and archaeologist who loves exploring ancient ruins and finding treasure. She travels with her adopted sister Brittany, a werecheetah warrior with a big heart and a bigger punch. Together they get into trouble with magic, monsters, and science. It's a lively pick for fans of fantasy adventure with plenty of humor.
328: My Hero Academia: School Briefs by Anri Yoshi (Viz Media) is a lighthearted light novel set in the world of My Hero Academia. The stories take place at U.A. High School between the big fights, following Class 1-A through dorm life, school events, and everyday moments. Readers get to see Deku and his classmates relax and goof around. It's a fun bonus for fans of the series who want more time with the characters.
331: The Demon Girl Next Door by Izumo Ito (Seven Seas) is a sweet fantasy comedy. Yuko Yoshida wakes up one morning with horns and a tail and learns that she comes from a line of demons. Her family is cursed with poverty, and the only way to break the curse is to defeat a magical girl. The problem is that Yuko is not very strong. It's a cozy, funny read for fans of gentle comedies.
332: The Elder Sister-Like One by Pochi Iida (Yen Press) is a supernatural romance. Yuu is a lonely boy who has lost his parents and is living with relatives who don't want him. When he finds a strange book and summons a demon, she takes on the form of an older sister and decides to look after him. The story is warm and a little odd, a good pick for readers who like slow, tender relationships.
333: Attack on Titan: Junior High by Saki Nakagawa (Kodansha) is a school comedy spin-off of Attack on Titan. Eren, Mikasa, Armin, and the rest of the cast are now students at a junior high that is shared with the Titans. Eren still holds a grudge against the Titans, but this time the battles are over lunch and school clubs. It's a goofy, affectionate parody for fans who want to see the characters in a lighter setting.
338: Hell Girl by Miyuki Eto (Del Rey) is a supernatural horror series told in short stories. Rumor says that if you enter a name on a website at midnight, the Hell Girl will send that person to hell. The price is that your own soul will go there too when you die. Each chapter follows someone pushed to the edge and deciding whether revenge is worth it. It's a dark, moody read for fans of spooky anthologies.
344: Hirano and Kagiura by Shou Harusono (Yen Press) is a sweet boys' love romance. Kagiura is a first-year student who gets a new roommate in the school dorm, the third-year Hirano. Living together, the two grow close, and Kagiura begins to realize his feelings run deeper than friendship. It's a gentle, slow-building story set in the same world as Sasaki and Miyano, a good fit for readers who enjoy soft romance.
347: Nyankees by Atsushi Okada (Yen Press) is an action comedy about stray cats. In a quiet neighborhood, the local cats are divided into rival gangs who fight for territory, just like teenage delinquents in a classic gang story. The cats have names, codes of honor, and big personalities, and their brawls play out like a school-yard showdown. It's a funny and unexpectedly exciting read for cat lovers and fans of tough-guy stories.
357: Bobobo-bo Bo-bobo by Yoshio Sawai (Viz Media) is a wildly silly action comedy. In the future, the evil Chrome Empire sends its Hair Hunters to shave everyone bald. Standing against them is Bobobo-bo Bo-bobo, a man with a huge blond afro who fights with the strange art of the Nose Hair Fist. The jokes are random, loud, and nonstop. It's perfect for readers who love absurd humor and parodies of fighting manga.
360: Captive Hearts by Matsuri Hino (Viz Media) is a romantic comedy with a fantasy twist. Megumi Kuroishi is a rich teenager whose family has served the Tokino family for generations because of an ancient curse. When Suzuka, the Tokino daughter, comes back into his life, the curse takes hold and Megumi finds himself compelled to serve her. It's a sweet, playful romance from the creator of Vampire Knight.
361: Is It Wrong to Try to Pick Up Girls in a Dungeon? Familia Chronicle: Episode Lyu by Fujino Omori (Yen Press) is a fantasy action spin-off of DanMachi. Lyu Leon is a quiet elf who works as a waitress at the Hostess of Fertility tavern in Orario. This story looks back at her past as an adventurer with the Astrea Familia, a group devoted to justice. It's a great pick for DanMachi fans who want more of Lyu's story.
367: Pokémon Adventures: Gold & Silver by Hidenori Kusaka (Viz Media) is an all-ages adventure set in the Johto region. Gold is a boy from New Bark Town who would rather play than go on a journey. That changes when a mysterious trainer named Silver steals a Pokémon from Professor Elm's lab, and Gold sets out to catch him. It's a fast, exciting story for young fans of the games and anyone who loves Pokémon battles.
369: Pretty Face by Yasuhiro Kano (Viz Media) is a romantic comedy with a ridiculous setup. Rando Masashi is a tough karate fighter who is badly hurt in a bus accident. The doctor who rebuilds his face uses a photo from his wallet, and Rando wakes up looking exactly like Rina, the girl he has a crush on. Soon he is living with her family, pretending to be her missing twin. It's a goofy, fast-paced comedy.
372: Tougen Anki: Legend of the Cursed Blood by Yura Urushibara (Yen Press) is a supernatural action series. Shiki Ichinose is a rebellious teen who learns that he carries the blood of oni. When the descendants of Momotaro, the legendary oni slayer, come to hunt him down, his life is turned upside down. He heads to a school that trains oni to fight back. It's a strong pick for fans of action series like Jujutsu Kaisen.
375: Real Bout High School by Reiji Saiga (Tokyopop) is an action comedy set at a very unusual school. At Daimon High, students settle their arguments with official fights called K-Fights. Ryoko Mikado is a kendo champion who has never lost, and she just wants a normal school life. When a mysterious transfer student shows up, things get a lot more complicated. It's a fun read for fans of school fighting stories.
380: Red String by Gina Biggs (Dark Horse) is a heartfelt romance drama. Miharu is a high school girl in Japan who learns that her parents have arranged a marriage for her with a young man she has never met. She is upset, especially since she has her own idea of love. As the two families get to know each other, feelings grow complicated. It's a sweet, emotional pick for readers who love slow-building romance.
386: Death Note Black Edition by Tsugumi Ohba and Takeshi Obata (Viz Media) is a dark psychological thriller. Light Yagami is a brilliant high school student who finds a notebook dropped by a death god. Anyone whose name is written in it will die. Light decides to use it to rid the world of criminals, and soon a genius detective known only as L is on his trail. It's a gripping cat-and-mouse story in a handsome collected edition.
387: Demon Love Spell by Mayu Shinjo (Viz Media) is a supernatural romantic comedy. Miko is a shrine maiden who wants to exorcise evil spirits, but she isn't very good at it. When she accidentally seals the powers of Kagura, a handsome and dangerous incubus, he is stuck in a weakened form and sticks around her. The two keep arguing even as their feelings grow. It's a fun pick for fans of fantasy romance.
390: Wild Adapter by Kazuya Minekura (Tokyopop) is a moody crime drama. Makoto Kubota is a laid-back young man who once had ties to the yakuza. One day he picks up Minoru Tokito, a stray with no memory and a strange, beast-like hand. Their meeting pulls them into the mystery of a dangerous drug called Wild Adapter. Gritty and stylish, it's a great choice for fans of Minekura's Saiyuki.
394: Laughing Under the Clouds by Karakara Kemuri (Tokyopop) is a historical action story set in early Meiji-era Japan. The carefree Tenka Kumou and his younger brothers guard prisoners as they are taken to Gokumonjo, a prison on Lake Biwa. Their family is also tied to a legend about the great serpent Orochi, which returns every few hundred years. It's a mix of family warmth and sword fighting, with lovely art.
395: Wonderland by Yugo Ishikawa (Seven Seas) is a survival horror story. Yukko wakes up one morning to find that she and her dog have shrunk to the size of a doll. Her parents have shrunk too, and the familiar world of her house and town has become huge and dangerous. Every ordinary thing could be a threat. It's a tense, creative read for fans of survival stories and strange fantasy.
397: Limit by Keiko Suenobu (Vertical) is a tense survival drama. Mizuki Konno is a high school girl who works hard to fit in with the popular crowd. On a class trip, a bus crash leaves only her and a handful of classmates alive in the woods, with no adults and no way home. As they struggle to survive, the school social order is turned upside down. It's gripping, thoughtful, and sometimes dark.
399: Samurai 8: The Tale of Hachimaru by Masashi Kishimoto (Viz Media) is a sci-fi samurai adventure from the creator of Naruto, with art by Akira Okubo. Hachimaru is a sickly boy who can't survive without life support and dreams of being strong. When a mysterious samurai cat arrives, he gets a chance to become a samurai himself. It's a short, imaginative series for fans of space adventures and big action.
